carousel.hook: You have been drinking chicory your entire life. The ingredient panel proves it.
carousel.title: How to Read a Coffee Label Like Someone Who Refuses Fillers

slides.heading: The ingredient panel is the only truth that matters
slides.body: Marketing lives on the front. Reality lives on the back. Flip any instant coffee jar. If the ingredient list reads 'Coffee, Chicory' or 'Coffee Blend', you are paying for roasted root filler. Purista's label reads: 'Instant Coffee (pure coffee)'. That is the entire list. Purity Beans has nothing to hide.
slides.visual: Extreme close-up of Purista 50g jar back panel — ingredient line sharp enough to read: 'Instant Coffee (pure coffee)'. Warm gold light catches the foil stamp. A thumb holds the jar naturally, slight pressure whitening the knuckle. Real hand, real jar. Skin pores visible. Dark marble background. Single fingerprint smudge on the glass shoulder.

slides.heading: Pure coffee behaves differently in cold milk — no chicory bite
slides.body: Chicory turns harsh and astringent the moment it hits cold temperature. Pure freeze-dried coffee does not. Purista is pure Robusta granules — zero chicory. When you make cold coffee with Purista, the finish stays clean: dark chocolate, toasted nut, no bitter ghost note. That is the pure-coffee difference you taste, not read about. Purity Beans makes it obvious.
slides.visual: Side-by-side in focus: left glass shows dark, muddy liquid with visible sediment (generic instant coffee implied). Right glass shows clear, rich amber Purista cold coffee over ice. Purista 50g jar prominent on right, label facing camera. Condensation beads on both glasses — real physics. Water ring on marble counter. Crumpled napkin at edge of frame. Morning light through window.

slides.heading: The two-spoon paste test reveals the process
slides.body: Two spoons Purista. Two spoons cold water. Stir 60 seconds until pale and thick. Watch the color: freeze-dried pure coffee turns golden-amber. Spray-dried or chicory-heavy blends turn flat brown. The difference is visible before milk touches it. This is how you verify freeze-dried quality at home. Purity Beans Purista: gourmet Robusta, zero chicory.
slides.visual: Close-up: a stainless spoon whipping a pale, thick coffee paste in the bottom of a glass. Purista 50g jar in background, slightly blurred but label readable. Natural steam rises. Fingerprints on the glass. Morning light catches the jar's shoulder. A few Purista granules rest on the glass rim — real texture. Charging cable peeking from counter edge.

slides.heading: Freeze-dried granules keep the aroma that spray drying loses
slides.body: Purista uses freeze-dried Robusta granules. The low-temperature process locks in volatile aromatics that high-heat spray drying destroys. Open the jar — the scent hits you before the spoon does. That locked-in aroma translates to a naturally rich crema and a smooth, bold cup every time. Purity Beans Purista: gourmet Robusta, zero chicory.
slides.visual: Purista 50g jar (glass, matte black label, gold foil accents) on dark marble. Lid off. A few granules mid-air, caught falling from spoon to jar — motion frozen. Warm amber backlight glows through the glass. Steam curls naturally. Charging cable peeking from counter edge. Lived-in realism. Slight oil sheen on fingertips holding spoon.

slides.heading: Cold milk emulsifies cleanly with pure coffee — no separation
slides.body: Pour cold milk over the Purista paste. Pure coffee emulsifies into a silky, stable swirl — oils and solids hold together. No separation. No sediment sinking. No oil rings floating. Stir once. The glass stays uniform to the last sip. This is what effortless cold coffee looks like when the jar contains only coffee. Purity Beans delivers it.
slides.visual: Milk pouring into the Purista paste — captured mid-swirl, amber and white dancing. Purista 50g jar beside the glass, catchlight on the gold foil. Ice cubes clink (implied motion blur). Kitchen counter shows life: crumpled napkin, phone face-down, charging cable. Real morning chaos, pure coffee calm. Slight condensation on jar.

linkedin_post.hook: Most distributors don't ask about margins first. They ask what's in the jar.
linkedin_post.body:
I've had 47 conversations with FMCG distributors in the last quarter. The pattern is consistent.

First question: "What's the ingredient list?"
Second: "Is it pure coffee or chicory blend?"
Third: "Can I show the label to a customer confidently?"

They know the shelf reality. Customers flip the jar. They read the back panel. They put it back if the label hides something.

Purity Beans gives them a straight answer:
• Bold — pure coffee, agglomerated, zero chicory
• Purista — pure Gourmet Robusta, freeze-dried granules, zero chicory
• Purica — pure Arabica, freeze-dried granules, zero chicory
• Ultra Blend — 70% coffee, 30% chicory, labeled honestly

No asterisks. No fine print. No "coffee flavour" masking fillers.

We're expanding our distributor network in Tier-1 and Tier-2 cities. Looking for partners who want a product the label defends itself.

If you distribute FMCG and this sounds like a shelf you want, let's talk.

threads_post.hook: Most people think Robusta instant coffee is harsh. They've never tasted freeze-dried Gourmet Robusta.
threads_post.body: Purista from Purity Beans is freeze-dried, not agglomerated. That means the aroma compounds survive the process instead of burning off in high-heat spray drying. The result: a Robusta that delivers bold caffeine kick with natural crema and zero chicory — ₹319 for 50g, ₹509 for 100g at https://p3online.in. No filler. No roasted root. Just pure coffee granules that dissolve clean.
threads_post.payoff: The difference isn't marketing. It's physics. Freeze-drying preserves what spray drying destroys.
threads_post.reply_ask: How do you take your instant coffee — black, with milk, or something else?
threads_post.share_ask: Send this to the friend who claims they don't like Robusta.
